notes: Strong run: ran the validator first, turned every RULE line into a numbered rule-referenced finding, asked targeted questions that each decide a relationship, and checked flips for new cycles (caught the Payments <-> Accounts side effect and asked about it). Critic use was proportionate. Cost: 430s vs 171s baseline, three expert rounds. Debatable call: City -> Pricing CF -> ACL reasoned as 'power fact, not a well-established language'; the trainer's rule could also accept CF to an imposed external format, so the skill might prompt the expert specifically on external CFs rather than deciding. The 'rule N' numbering in discovery.md refers to the skill's internal rule list; the user-facing final message names rules in prose only, which is fine. The expert's 'Expert reply' blocks appear twice (message + hand-back) - harmless transcript duplication. Eval weakness: assertions 1-4 are mostly satisfied by the validator script output alone; an assertion that checks the proposed fix (e.g. the cycle-break direction is expert-confirmed) would be more discriminating.
